gloss: haniwa; clay figure from ancient Japan

definitions.explanation: Unglazed terracotta figures that were placed on and around burial mounds ({古墳|こふん}) during the Kofun period (3rd–6th century). They depict humans, animals, houses and other objects.

examples.japanese: {埴輪|はにわ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出土|しゅつど}→出土：11760_shutsudo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{博物館|はくぶつかん}→博物館：01494_hakubutsukan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{馬|うま}→馬：01865_uma⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{形|かたち}→形：02193_katachi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧{埴輪|はにわ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: I saw a horse-shaped haniwa at the museum.

examples.japanese: {埴輪|はにわ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{古墳|こふん}{時代|じだい}→古墳時代：23333_kofunjidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人々|ひとびと}→人々：03141_hitobito⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{暮|く}らし→暮らし：02670_kurashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{知|し}る→知る：00458_shiru⟧{手|て}がかり⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なっている→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Haniwa serve as clues to understanding the lives of people in the Kofun period.

notes:
Haniwa were set in rows on and around the ⟦{古墳|こふん}→古墳：11853_kofun⟧ (burial mounds) of the ⟦{古墳|こふん}{時代|じだい}→古墳時代：23333_kofunjidai⟧ (Kofun period).

TYPES:
- ⟦{円筒|えんとう}→円筒：15435_entou⟧{埴輪|はにわ}: cylindrical haniwa (the most numerous)
- ⟦{人物|じんぶつ}→人物：03356_jinbutsu⟧{埴輪|はにわ}: human figures
- ⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧{埴輪|はにわ}: animals, such as horses

CULTURAL NOTE:
The round hollow eyes and open mouths of human haniwa are instantly recognized in Japan and turn up in mascots and cartoons.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{土偶|どぐう}→土偶：12370_doguu⟧: clay figurine of the much earlier Jomon period — a different object, often confused with haniwa
